title: Module Header: AEP Problem Statement and Development History
content: The module opens with the open question from `shannon-source-coding-oq-03`: can the AEP be formalized using Mathlib's probability infrastructure? It defines empirical entropy empEnt(x) = -(1/n)∑log p(xᵢ) = -(1/n)log P(x₁,...,xₙ) and states the McMillan (1953) theorem: P(|empEnt - H| > ε) ≤ Var[-log p]/nε². The 'Mathematical Status' section at lines 36-40 is a historical artifact recording the original sorry structure — noting that `expVal_marginal` and `empEnt_variance` were unproved when the file was first committed. These sorries were subsequently eliminated in PR #15161. The module header connects AEP to source coding: the typical set T_ε^(n) has |T_ε| ≤ exp(n(H+ε)), enabling compression to rate H(p).
mathContext: AEP: $\Pr\left(\left|\frac{-\log P(\mathbf{X}_1^n)}{n} - H(p)\right| > \varepsilon\right) \leq \frac{\mathrm{Var}_p[-\log p(X)]}{n\varepsilon^2}$. Empirical entropy: $\mathrm{empEnt}(\mathbf{x}) = -\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \log p(x_i)$. McMillan's theorem (1953) first proved this almost surely; the Chebyshev approach here gives explicit finite-$n$ rates.
prerequisites: Shannon entropy H(p) = -∑ p log p

title: Discrete Probability Distribution and Entropy Non-negativity
content: A probability distribution on a finite alphabet of size k: a function p : Fin k → ℝ with p(i) ≥ 0 for all i and ∑ p(i) = 1. The Lean formulation as a `structure` bundles the function with its proofs, avoiding MeasureTheory overhead for a self-contained treatment. `shannonH_nonneg` proves H(D) ≥ 0 by noting p(i) ∈ [0,1] implies log p(i) ≤ 0, so each term -p(i) log p(i) ≥ 0. The proof uses `Finset.single_le_sum` to bound p(i) ≤ ∑ p = 1.
mathContext: H(D) = -\sum_{i} p(i) \log p(i) \geq 0 since $p(i) \in [0,1]$ implies $\log p(i) \leq 0$, so each summand $-p(i)\log p(i) \geq 0$.

title: Shannon Entropy: Convention 0 log 0 = 0
content: H(D) = -∑ p(i) log p(i), with the convention 0 log 0 = 0 (encoded as `if D.p i = 0 then 0 else ...`). This convention is necessary because log p(i) is undefined when p(i) = 0. In Lean, Real.log 0 = 0 by convention, so `D.p i * Real.log (D.p i)` would be 0 when p(i) = 0 anyway — but the explicit `if` makes the intent clear and avoids reliance on this coincidence.
mathContext: H(D) = -\sum_{i} p(i) \log p(i)$ where $0 \cdot \log 0 := 0$ by convention (the limit $\lim_{p \to 0^+} p \log p = 0$).

title: Joint i.i.d. Distribution: Product Measure Without Measure Theory
content: P(x₁,...,xₙ) = ∏ᵢ p(xᵢ). This is the product measure for i.i.d. random variables, encoded directly as a finite product. `jointProb_nonneg` follows from non-negativity of p and `Finset.prod_nonneg`. The design choice to avoid MeasureTheory is deliberate: it makes all proofs elementary and keeps the formalization self-contained at the undergraduate level. The type `Fin n → Fin k` represents all n-length sequences over the k-symbol alphabet.
prerequisites: Fin n → Fin k as sequence type

title: Normalization: Joint Probability Sums to 1 via Induction
content: ∑_{x : Fin n → Fin k} ∏ᵢ p(xᵢ) = 1. Proved by induction on n: the base case n=0 is trivial (empty product = 1). The successor step uses `Fintype.sum_piFinset_succ` to peel off the first coordinate, then `Fin.prod_univ_succ` to factor the product, and finally the inductive hypothesis plus D.sum_one. This induction on sequence length is the discrete Fubini theorem: the product measure is normalized.
prerequisites: induction on natural numbers in Lean 4

title: Empirical Entropy: The Sample Average of Surprisal
content: empEnt(x) := -(1/n) ∑ᵢ log p(xᵢ) = -(1/n) log P(x). This is the average surprisal, or negative log-probability per symbol. The lemma `empEnt_eq_neg_log_joint` makes the connection to the joint probability explicit: empEnt(x) = -(1/n) log P(x) when all p(xᵢ) > 0, proved via `Real.log_prod`. The AEP says this average concentrates around H(p) as n → ∞.

title: Expected Value Over the Joint Distribution
content: expVal D n f = ∑_{x : Fin n → Fin k} P(x) · f(x). This defines the expected value of any function f of the n-length sequence. The key design: the domain is `Fin n → Fin k`, a Fintype, making the sum finite and all manipulations algebraic (no measurability required). All subsequent lemmas — marginal factorization, entropy mean, variance — are expressed in terms of expVal.
prerequisites: function type Fin n → Fin k

title: Marginal Factorization: The Algebraic Core of i.i.d.
content: E[g(Xⱼ)] = ∑_a p(a)·g(a) for any function g and coordinate j. This lemma encodes independence: in an i.i.d. sequence, the marginal distribution of any single coordinate Xⱼ is p, regardless of j. The proof strategy: rewrite (∏ᵢ p(xᵢ))·g(xⱼ) = ∏ᵢ hᵢ(xᵢ) where hᵢ = p·g on coordinate j, else p. Then Fintype.prod_sum (in reverse) exchanges sum-over-sequences with product-over-coordinates. The j-th factor gives ∑_a p(a)g(a); all other factors give ∑_a p(a) = 1.
mathContext: \mathbb{E}[g(X_j)] = \sum_{\mathbf{x}} P(\mathbf{x}) \cdot g(x_j) = \prod_{i \neq j} \left(\sum_a p(a)\right) \cdot \left(\sum_a p(a) g(a)\right) = \sum_a p(a) g(a).

title: Fintype.prod_sum: The Discrete Fubini Theorem
content: The key identity: ∏_a (∑_b f(a,b)) = ∑_{g:α→β} ∏_a f(a, g(a)). Applied in reverse: a sum over all functions x : Fin n → Fin k of a product-over-coordinates factors into a product of independent single-coordinate sums. This is exactly the i.i.d. property in algebraic form — each coordinate contributes independently to the product. The one-line `rw [← Fintype.prod_sum h]` is the heart of the `expVal_marginal` proof.
mathContext: \prod_{\alpha} \sum_{\beta} f(\alpha, \beta) = \sum_{g: \alpha \to \beta} \prod_{\alpha} f(\alpha, g(\alpha))$. In the AEP context: $\sum_{\mathbf{x}} \prod_i h_i(x_i) = \prod_i \sum_a h_i(a).

title: E[empEnt] = H(p): The LLN Heart of AEP
content: E[empEnt(X₁,...,Xₙ)] = H(p). Proof: expand empEnt = -(1/n)∑ᵢ log p(Xᵢ), apply linearity to get -(1/n)∑ᵢ E[log p(Xᵢ)]. By expVal_marginal with g = log ∘ p, each E[log p(Xᵢ)] = ∑_a p(a) log p(a). Summing n equal terms: -(1/n)·n·∑_a p(a) log p(a) = H(p). This is the LLN property: empEnt is an average of n i.i.d. terms each with expectation H(p).

title: Chebyshev's Inequality for Finite Distributions
content: P(|f(X)-μ| > ε) ≤ E[(f(X)-μ)²]/ε². Proved elementarily: on the event {|f(x)-μ| > ε}, we have ε² ≤ (f(x)-μ)², so ε² * P(event) ≤ ∑_{|f-μ|>ε} P(x)·(f(x)-μ)² ≤ E[(f-μ)²]. The Lean proof uses `le_div_iff` to rearrange, then `Finset.sum_le_sum` for the pointwise bound, and `Finset.sum_le_univ_sum_of_nonneg` to extend from filtered sum to full expectation.

title: logVar and 2D Independence: expVal_marginal_product
content: `logVar D` is the variance of the single-symbol surprisal: Var[-log p(X)] = E[(log p(X))²] - H(p)². The private lemma `expVal_marginal_product` extends marginal factorization to two distinct coordinates: for j₁ ≠ j₂, E[g₁(X_{j₁}) · g₂(X_{j₂})] = E[g₁] · E[g₂]. This bilinear independence fact is proved by a 2D extension of `expVal_marginal`: extract j₁ and j₂ from the product via two calls to `Finset.mul_prod_erase`, then apply `Fintype.prod_sum`. All remaining factors contribute ∑_a p(a) = 1.
mathContext: \mathrm{logVar}(D) = \mathbb{E}[(\log p(X))^2] - H(p)^2 = \mathrm{Var}[-\log p(X)]$. Independence: $j_1 \neq j_2 \Rightarrow \mathbb{E}[g_1(X_{j_1}) \cdot g_2(X_{j_2})] = \mathbb{E}[g_1] \cdot \mathbb{E}[g_2].

title: Variance of empEnt = logVar/n: The Crucial Calculation
content: E[(empEnt - H)²] = logVar D / n. This is the variance of the sample mean of n i.i.d. Zᵢ = -log p(Xᵢ) - H with mean 0 and variance logVar. The Lean proof expands (empEnt - H)² = (1/n)² · (∑ᵢ Zᵢ)² and splits into diagonal (i=j) and off-diagonal (i≠j) terms. Diagonal: E[Z(Xᵢ)²] = logVar by `expVal_marginal`. Off-diagonal: E[Z(Xᵢ)·Z(Xⱼ)] = E[Z]² = 0 by `expVal_marginal_product` + mean-centering. Sum: n·logVar diagonal + 0 off-diagonal, times (1/n)², gives logVar/n.

title: AEP Concentration Bound: Chebyshev Applied to empEnt
content: P(|empEnt - H| > ε) ≤ logVar(D)/(n·ε²). The proof is a two-step `calc`: first apply `chebyshev_finite` to get ≤ Var[empEnt]/ε², then substitute `empEnt_variance` (E[(empEnt-H)²] = logVar/n) to get logVar/(n·ε²). Historical note: the original version incorrectly used `expVal_empEnt` (which rewrites E[empEnt] = H, not the variance) — the fix was to use `empEnt_variance` instead.

title: Typical Set: Definition and Size Upper Bound
content: `typicalSet D n ε` is the set of sequences with |empEnt - H| ≤ ε. `typical_prob_lower_bound` shows each x ∈ T_ε has P(x) ≥ exp(-n(H+ε)) — by typicality, empEnt(x) ≤ H+ε, so -log P(x) = n·empEnt(x) ≤ n(H+ε). `typical_set_size_upper` follows: |T_ε| · exp(-n(H+ε)) ≤ ∑_{x∈T_ε} P(x) ≤ 1, so |T_ε| ≤ exp(n(H+ε)). This is the achievability direction of Shannon's source coding theorem.
mathContext: T_\varepsilon^{(n)} = \{\mathbf{x} : |\mathrm{empEnt}(\mathbf{x}) - H| \leq \varepsilon\}$. For $\mathbf{x} \in T_\varepsilon$: $P(\mathbf{x}) \geq e^{-n(H+\varepsilon)}$. Hence $|T_\varepsilon^{(n)}| \leq e^{n(H+\varepsilon)}.

title: Concrete Example: Fair Coin (uniformBin) with H = log 2
content: `uniformBin` is the fair coin distribution: p(0) = p(1) = 1/2 on Fin 2. `uniformBin_entropy` proves H(uniformBin) = log 2 using `Fin.sum_univ_two` and `Real.log_one_div`. This is the textbook sanity check: the binary entropy is log 2 ≈ 0.693 nats (or 1 bit in base-2 log). The AEP says long sequences of fair coin flips will have empirical entropy close to log 2.

title: Section VIII: Bug Fix Record — Variance vs Mean in Chebyshev
content: The closing summary documents a subtle proof repair that reveals a common pitfall in formalizing concentration inequalities. The original `aep_concentration` proof used `rw [expVal_empEnt]`, which rewrites E[empEnt] = H(p) — the mean identity. But Chebyshev's inequality bounds P(|X - μ| > ε) ≤ Var[X]/ε² — it needs the variance, not the mean. The fix was `rw [empEnt_variance]`, which rewrites E[(empEnt - H)²] = logVar/n. The original rewrite would have introduced H into the expression without actually bounding the fluctuations. This is a pedagogically important bug: the mean and variance are both correct equalities, but only the variance is relevant for the Chebyshev application.
mathContext: Wrong: `rw [expVal_empEnt]` uses $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{empEnt}] = H$ — this rewrites $H$ in the expression but does not bound $\mathrm{Var}[\mathrm{empEnt}]$. Correct: `rw [empEnt_variance]` uses $\mathbb{E}[(\mathrm{empEnt}-H)^2] = \mathrm{logVar}/n$, which IS the numerator in Chebyshev: $\Pr(|\mathrm{empEnt}-H| > \varepsilon) \leq \mathbb{E}[(\mathrm{empEnt}-H)^2]/\varepsilon^2 = \mathrm{logVar}/(n\varepsilon^2)$.
